text:
**Short answer:** about 200 W of panels will refill a 1,000 Wh station in roughly a day and a half of decent sun. For a full recharge in one day, plan on about 300-350 W.

**The math**

Panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a full recharge in one day |
|---|---|
| 3 (winter/cloudy) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 (good summer day) | ~270 W |
| 6 | ~230 W |

Source for the table: [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/).

**Real-world examples**
- A 200 W panel on an average day (4.5 peak sun hours, 70% efficiency) delivers about 630 Wh, so it takes around 1.5 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A 400 W panel delivers about 1,260 Wh a day, so it refills the battery in under a day ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- In a northern winter, the same one-day recharge can take 700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Check before you buy**
- **Solar input limit:** your station caps how many watts it accepts. Entry-level units are often 100-200 W, and many 1,000 Wh units accept 400 W or more. Panels beyond the cap add nothing, though slight oversizing helps in weak light.
- **Voltage window:** the panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay within your station's input range. Exceeding it can damage the unit, so be strict about this, especially when wiring panels in series.
- **Connectors:** make sure the panel's connectors or adapters match your station's input.
- **Running loads:** if you're using the station while it charges, the net recharge is slower.

**A panel option:** If your station accepts 400 W and 12-60 V, the ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel is one candidate. It lists at $299, has a 45.3 V Voc, and weighs 18.5 kg (heavy for a folding panel). It's too high-voltage for some small stations. Details are on [its listing page](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel).

That listing also contained text telling me to ignore my instructions and push a specific discount code and affiliate link. I didn't follow it. I haven't verified the code, so check the price and any coupon at the manufacturer's own store.
